summary: To help the first human astronauts navigate Mars safely and efficiently, Schrodinger’s map is an interactive web tool that helps a human explorer plan a walk across the Jezero Crater delta on Mars. It combines a terrain model built from USGS and MRO HiRISE elevation data, the software translates complex planetary datasets into an accessible, Google Maps style interface. Through the Marswalk Planner, astronauts can toggle between terrain imagery and slope layers and evaluate specific points along their journey. We created this software to help prevent fatal navigation errors during Martian surface operations.
details:
Building Schrodinger’s Map required solving a massive data scaling challenge: processing and rendering planetary scale terrain models containing over 1.5 billion elevation points without sacrificing safety. To be able to achieve this, we developed a separated high performance backend routing engine from an intuitive web-based frontend interface. 

The core backend was engineered in Java, chosen for its efficiency in handling custom raster handling, complex data structures, JSON writers, and HTTP servers. We integrated raw planetary data sourced from NASA PDS/MEDIA archives, USGS, and MRO HiRISE elevation models, processing them alongside QGIS map data to accurately map the Jezero Crater delta topography. Because querying raw 1.5 billion point datasets in real time for pathfinding is near impossible, we implemented a unique two stage routing system.

Stage 1: An initial A pathfinding algorithm rapidly computes a baseline route across a compressed version of the regional data.

Stage 2: Once the general trajectory is established, the system generates a local high resolution corridor around the path. Within this targeted zone, it processes fine grained elevation and slope data to optimize the route, actively avoiding dangerous steep slows while keeping total route inflation under one percent.

On the client side, we translated these complex geospatial matrices into an accessible, Google Maps style web application known as the Marswalker Planner. The frontend allows users to seamlessly toggle between different visual layers such as terrain imagery and slope maps. By bridging rigorous backend data processing with a clean, responsive web interface, Schrodinger’s Map transforms dense multi-mission scientific archives into an actionable, real time mission planning tool to prevent navigation errors during Martian surface operations.
